title: Default Servicing Basis for Home Mortgage Loans During and at the End of a Forbearance Plan
content:
While a Home Mortgage Loans note stands in forbearance, three things hold of it: interest continues to accrue, escrow bills continue to be paid, and no late charges are assessed on it.

When the plan ends, the loan returns to active where the deferred amounts were repaid, or were moved into a repayment plan, a deferral or a modification by the loss mitigation team. Otherwise it goes to delinquent.

Choosing among a repayment plan, a deferral and a modification is a loss mitigation decision, and lies outside this policy.

## During the plan

| Element of servicing | Position while the plan runs |
|---|---|
| Interest | Continues to accrue |
| Escrow bills | Continue to be paid |
| Late charges | None are assessed |

## At the end of the plan

| The position of the deferred amounts when the plan ends | Where the loan stands afterwards |
|---|---|
| Repaid | Active |
| Moved into a repayment plan, a deferral or a modification by the loss mitigation team | Active |
| Neither of those | Delinquent |

## Points of judgement

The two routes back to active are alternatives, and either of them on its own carries the loan there. Where neither holds when the plan ends, the loan is delinquent, and which of a repayment plan, a deferral or a modification a borrower might have been offered is a matter the loss mitigation team decides on its own basis.
